key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 steel, delivering the best protection among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: The coating offers a promising route to protect SA516 boiler steel against high-temperature oxidation through a dense protective oxide layer.
method: Apply Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing showed severe oxide spalling and cracking on bare steel, while the best-performing coating reduced weight gain by 95.71% and formed protective oxide phases.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory cycles does not establish long-term durability in boiler environments containing corrosive gases and deposits.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
